scenes.visual: Title card: Engine and Clutch.

scenes.tts: How can the edge of a growth cone move forward while its actin network streams backward?
scenes.visual: Top-down growth cone with red actin speckles streaming from the edge toward the centre. Title card: Engine and clutch.
scenes.narration: How can the edge of a growth cone move forward while its actin network streams backward?

scenes.tts: Look inside the fan. New actin joins the filaments at the front edge.
scenes.visual: Close-up of the leading edge: new red subunits add at filament ends facing the edge.
scenes.narration: Look inside the fan. New actin joins the filaments at the front edge.

scenes.tts: Myosin two pulls the network back toward the centre. Its own assembly pushes it back too.
scenes.visual: Myosin motors tug the mesh backward; arrows at the membrane show the push of assembly.
scenes.caption: Myosin II pulls the network back toward the centre. Its own assembly pushes it back too.
scenes.narration: Myosin II pulls the network back toward the centre. Its own assembly pushes it back too.

scenes.tts: Near the centre, the filaments are taken apart. This backward movement is called retrograde flow.
scenes.visual: Speckles stream back and fade near the centre. Label: retrograde flow.
scenes.narration: Near the centre, the filaments are taken apart. This backward movement is called retrograde flow.

scenes.tts: In 1988, Paul Forscher and Stephen Smith filmed this in a sea slug with giant, flat growth cones.
scenes.visual: A sea slug, then its large flat growth cone in culture. Label: Aplysia growth cone; Forscher and Smith, 1988.
scenes.narration: In 1988, Paul Forscher and Stephen Smith filmed this in a sea slug with giant, flat growth cones.

scenes.tts: They added cytochalasin, a drug that stops actin adding at the front edge.
scenes.visual: A drug wash enters. Label: cytochalasin blocks addition at the edge.
scenes.narration: They added cytochalasin, a drug that stops actin adding at the front edge.

scenes.tts: Addition at the front stops. What happens to the actin just behind the edge?
scenes.visual: Addition at the edge is blocked; question mark over the actin band.
scenes.narration: Addition at the front stops. What happens to the actin just behind the edge?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: An empty band opens at the front and widens. The rest of the network keeps moving back.
scenes.visual: A dark actin-free band opens at the front and widens as the speckles keep streaming back.
scenes.narration: An empty band opens at the front and widens. The rest of the network keeps moving back.

scenes.tts: So the flow was there all along. Addition at the front had been hiding it.
scenes.visual: Caption card: the flow was always there.
scenes.narration: So the flow was there all along. Addition at the front had been hiding it.

scenes.tts: Then the microtubules push forward into the emptied band. The actin had been holding them back.
scenes.visual: Green microtubules creep forward from the centre into the dark band.
scenes.narration: Then the microtubules push forward into the emptied band. The actin had been holding them back.

scenes.visual: Before and after panels side by side, matching the cytochalasin figure.

scenes.tts: So why does the edge ever advance? In 1988, Tim Mitchison and Marc Kirschner proposed a clutch.
scenes.visual: Label: the clutch hypothesis, Mitchison and Kirschner, 1988.
scenes.narration: So why does the edge ever advance? In 1988, Tim Mitchison and Marc Kirschner proposed a clutch.

scenes.tts: Think of the actin network as a running engine, and the ground as the road.
scenes.visual: The actin mesh drawn as a running engine above a road surface. This picture is for moving forward only.
scenes.narration: Think of the actin network as a running engine, and the ground as the road.

scenes.tts: If actin is added and carried back at the same rate, the engine runs, and the edge goes nowhere.
scenes.visual: Two equal bars: added and carried back. The edge marker stays still. Label: clutch disengaged.
scenes.narration: If actin is added and carried back at the same rate, the engine runs, and the edge goes nowhere.

scenes.tts: Adhesion molecules can link the network to the ground. Then the clutch engages, and the backward flow slows.
scenes.visual: Adhesion molecules under the fan grab the surface; speckles above the grip slow down.
scenes.narration: Adhesion molecules can link the network to the ground. Then the clutch engages, and the backward flow slows.

scenes.tts: If building stays the same, it now pushes the edge forward.
scenes.visual: The edge bulges forward above the grip.
scenes.narration: If building stays the same, it now pushes the edge forward.

scenes.tts: Put it as bookkeeping. Advance equals actin added at the edge, minus actin carried back.
scenes.visual: On screen: rate of advance = rate of addition − rate of retrograde flow.
scenes.narration: Put it as bookkeeping. Advance equals actin added at the edge, minus actin carried back.

scenes.tts: Suter and colleagues made the grip themselves. They held a bead coated with an adhesion molecule against the edge.
scenes.visual: A small bead coated with adhesion molecules is held against the edge. Label: Suter and colleagues, 1998.
scenes.narration: Suter and colleagues made the grip themselves. They held a bead coated with an adhesion molecule against the edge.

scenes.tts: Behind the bead, the backward flow slowed.
scenes.visual: Speckles in line with the bead slow almost to a stop.
scenes.narration: Behind the bead, the backward flow slowed.

scenes.tts: With illustrative numbers, flow falls from three and a half to half a micrometre a minute. Building stays the same, so the edge moves seven times faster.
scenes.visual: Two-bar panel. Before: added 4.0, flow 3.5, advance 0.5. Under the bead: added 4.0, flow 0.5, advance 3.5 micrometres per minute. Label: illustrative values.
scenes.narration: With illustrative numbers, flow falls from three and a half to half a micrometre a minute. Building stays the same, so the edge moves seven times faster.

scenes.tts: Now make the grip, or the building, unequal across the two sides of the cone.
scenes.visual: The fan splits into left and right halves with different grip icons.
scenes.narration: Now make the grip, or the building, unequal across the two sides of the cone.

scenes.tts: Carry one idea. Grip can speed the edge just by holding back the flow, with no faster building.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: grip holds back the flow; the same building moves the edge further.
scenes.narration: Carry one idea. Grip can speed the edge just by holding back the flow, with no faster building.

scenes.visual: End card.
